evidence:
The proposed local queue sequence is credible, but it does not complete the required demonstration against the selected contract. At the reviewed tip, InvitationContext::wakes (src/delivery/invitation.rs:110-111) classifies timed/required invitation offers as waking; register.js:296-313 preserves that classification. Its attention_cleared handler (243-256) retracts only non-inflight Attention for the named presentation epoch, so a previously received timed invitation remains queued. With no open turn, no abort/backoff hold and an empty composer, pump (431-462), passive (540), and deliverIdle (471-520) can append that invitation and submit the content-free wake. delivery.test.ts:1911-1919 independently specifies that a timed invitation alone may wake; this review did not execute a runtime reproduction.

The final contradiction asserted by the finding is unsupported. The root invitation contract (2026-10-10-handoff-delivery-redesign-design.md:30-34) requires canonical acceptance settlement, mode-aware delivery and guarded timed attention; it does not promise cancellation of previously emitted invitation offers. The parent-selected framing refinement, explicitly incorporated by root design:150-152, states at task-15-framing-refinement-proposal.md:277 that a scoped clear removes only the old epoch's unsent JS item/run key and remains valid even when a newer episode is open. It is not a global indication that every other queued waking item has become ineligible. The same selected proposal:299 explicitly accepts already-inflight, emitted or appended downstream content with no retraction or model-consumption promise. TRUST-POLICY.md:1524-1528 defines FULL OFFER as complete stdout write/flush, not model uptake or acceptance. src/cli/watch.rs:681-700 physically writes/flushes invitation lines before canonical presentation confirmation, so an invitation already in this JS queue is already emitted under those semantics even if the draft has postponed append/wake.

Canonical acceptance itself is implemented (src/store/control.rs:1112-1114); subsequent invitation replay hydrates through digest_pending_invitations (invitation_content.rs:525), checks current context (1728-1730), and retires invalid descriptors (1742-1744). Exact Absent creates the scoped passive clear (2186-2189; Controls::absent at 1413-1424). Receiving that clear removes its unsent Attention rather than issuing a new wake. A later wake attributable to an earlier timed invitation offer demonstrates the expressly bounded downstream behavior, not continued canonical invitation obligation or a waking clear. To confirm as a defect would require an additional stated guarantee that a cleared Attention episode revokes the wake eligibility of already emitted invitation contexts; the selected spec instead scopes retraction and accepts emitted downstream content. This is internal source reasoning; no external-world premise or external research is needed.
